errors.english: the observation that things like a rabbit's horns do not exist serves to prove that the subject, space, likewise does not exist
errors.why: The Tibetan says that this reason (being unproduced), since it is seen in non-existents such as a rabbit's horn, proves that the subject space is non-existent; it is the reason that is observed in non-existents, not an observation that rabbit horns do not exist.

fix.find: the observation that things like a rabbit's horns do not exist serves to prove that the subject, space, likewise does not exist
fix.replace: this [reason], since it is observed in non-existent things such as a rabbit's horns, proves that the subject, space, too does not exist

note: Accurate rendering of the svayam/iṣṭa discussion except for the misread rabbit-horn example.

errors.english: [note: This likely refers to Lake Manasarovar or a similar sacred body of water mentioned in Vinaya commentaries.]
errors.why: The commentary only says the lake is named after a water-pot; the identification with Manasarovar is unsupported speculation.

errors.english: because it surpasses the noble ones, it causes beings to progress
errors.why: The instrumental དམ་པས marks the excellent ones as those who make it proceed / by whom it is distinguished; it does not say the aeon surpasses the noble ones.

note: A word-gloss commentary rendered sensibly; a speculative note and one inverted case relation.

errors.english: but for the sake of realizing these afflictions, there is awakening
errors.why: The sūtra says awakening is so called because these afflictions are understood (awakening consists in understanding them), not that awakening exists for the purpose of realizing them.

note: Faithful rendering of the commentary and the Akṣayamatinirdeśa quotation, with one doubtful causal clause.
A careful rendering of the Vinaya discussion of the building rule and the Pṛcchā citation.

errors.english: Because his words are encountered by noble beings, they are like those of a high-born person.
errors.why: སྐྱེས here is 'gift': when he meets noble people his words become like a gift.

fix.find: Because his words are encountered by noble beings, they are like those of a high-born person.
fix.replace: Because when he meets noble people, his words become like a gift.

note: The compound analyses are followed well; the opening simile is misread.

errors.english: one must quickly be assisted and supported in separating from the injury and moving away from the punishment by the community of monks (Sangha)
errors.why: The disciple is the one who must help and support the preceptor or teacher who has the offense, so that he is quickly freed from the Saṅgha's punishment and harm.

fix.find: one must quickly be assisted and supported in separating from the injury and moving away from the punishment by the community of monks (Sangha)
fix.replace: the student must help and support him so that he is quickly freed from the punishment and other harm imposed by the community of monks (Sangha)

errors.english: it means to be separated from the state of dependence [note: original: "མནོད་པ་" the state of being under a tutor's instruction]
errors.why: The commentary glosses མནོད་པ as གནོད་པ, harm (the Saṅgha's punitive action), not the state of dependence.

errors.english: The dependent also performs these duties for the teacher, with the exception of questioning.
errors.why: The section explains the duties of the niśraya-teacher: he too must do these things for the dependent, except asking permission.

fix.find: The dependent also performs these duties for the teacher, with the exception of questioning.
fix.replace: He [the teacher of dependence] too must do these things for him, except for asking permission.

errors.english: This means that while the one in dependence should not interrogate the teacher, they must assist and support the teacher
errors.why: The niśraya-teacher too, except that he need not ask permission, must help the dependent with bowl, robes and so on.

fix.find: This means that while the one in dependence should not interrogate the teacher, they must assist and support the teacher
fix.replace: This means that the teacher of dependence, too, except that he need not ask permission, must assist and support the dependent

errors.english: Not if they lack even one of the qualities mentioned in the sets of five.
errors.why: The rule excludes one who possesses none of the sets of five, as the commentary itself goes on to say, not one who lacks any single quality.

fix.find: Not if they lack even one of the qualities mentioned in the sets of five.
fix.replace: Not one who possesses none of the sets of five described below.

note: The second half (the four abilities) is good, but the duties of the dependence-giver are reversed into duties of the dependent, and the opening agent is wrong.

errors.english: refers to the presentation of the Samkhya [note: A dualist school of Indian philosophy.]
errors.why: In context the 'and so on' introduces the enumerated items, colour and the rest, not the Sāṃkhya school.

errors.english: how there could be no pervading presence [note: term: (anvaya) logical pervasion or positive concomitance]
errors.why: Here རྗེས་སུ་འགྲོ་བ is the universal's running through its individuals (anugama), not logical positive concomitance.

note: Follows a terse pratīka-by-pratīka commentary but the later lines become garbled and the notes mislead.

errors.why: ཕྱི་རོལ་པ་རྣམས here means the external things (svalakṣaṇas), as the next sentence explains, not externalist philosophers.

note: The apoha argument is followed well; one term is misread as a school.
An accurate rendering of the trairūpya and asiddha discussion, including the Digambara example.

errors.english: it consists of various qualities such as blue and so forth
errors.why: ལྡན་པ is the Vaiśeṣika quality saṃyoga, conjunction: the opponent posits a variegated conjunction of blue and the rest; it is rendered 'qualities' here and 'possession' throughout.

fix.find: it consists of various qualities such as blue and so forth
fix.replace: there is a variegated conjunction (saṃyoga) of blue and so forth

errors.english: It is not correct to understand that the perception is produced by [note: a single whole].
errors.why: The rejected claim is that the cognition is produced by that conjunction, not by a single whole.

errors.english: the object of sound is not diverse in nature
errors.why: སྒྲ is 'word': the conjunction that is the referent of the word 'variegated' is not variegated in nature.

errors.english: [note: original: "gzugs med", meaning it lacks substantial visible form as a single unit]
errors.why: གཟུགས is the quality colour (rūpa); conjunction, being a quality, cannot carry the quality colour, as the next sentence says.

note: The dialectic is tracked, but the key Vaiśeṣika term saṃyoga is rendered as 'possession' throughout, which obscures the argument.
